newsitem.title: UK: New opinion polls dismiss Labour plunge as freak.
newsitem.headline: New opinion polls dismiss Labour plunge as freak.

text.p: Three new opinion polls released late on Wednesday appeared to dismiss an ICM survey earlier in the day which showed the opposition Labour Party's lead plunging to five points from 14.
The polls for Channel Four television and two newspapers, The Times and The Daily Telegraph, put Labour's lead over the ruling Conservatives at 19 points, 21 points and 20 points respectively.
The Gallup poll for the Channel Four news showed Labour's lead down four points from a week ago, and the Telegraph's daily rolling poll by Gallup put Labour down one point.
But the MORI poll for The Times showed Labour's lead had widened in the past week.
The Channel Four poll gave Labour 50 percent of the vote, down four points, while the Conservatives were unchanged at 31 percent.
The Telegraph poll put Labour at 50 percent, down one point from a day earlier, while the Conservatives were again unchanged at 30 points.
The Times poll put support for Labour at 48 percent, down one point from a week ago, while the Conservatives fell five points to 27 percent. This was the Conservatives' worst result since mid-March.
Labour, which needs a 4.3 percent swing to win the May 1 election, has held on to a double-digit opinion poll lead for at least the last 18 months.
Earlier in the five-week-old election campaign, its lead had reached 28 points, but recent polls had shown this slipping.
The ICM poll in Wednesday's Guardian, could if accurate have thrown the election race wide open and Channel Four's survey showed Labour cannot relax yet.
Gallup said half of voters have not yet made up their minds which way they will vote.
It showed that if voters who said they may not turn out on voting day and those who might still change their mind were subtracted, Labour's lead fell to 12 points.
